skills.name: game-design:game-content-design
skills.description: Design, revise or generate a game repertoire of encounters, items, places, scenes or other related content. Use when meaningful differences, compatibility, repetition, eligibility, selection or presentation determine what players can encounter. Skip an isolated object with no set-level question, decorative renaming and generic text generation unrelated to game state.

interface.shortDescription: Build meaningful repertoires and content selection
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-content-design to create playable content variations and show how they are selected and presented.

skills.name: game-design:game-design
skills.description: Create and develop a game concept, reconcile interacting game decisions, or adapt an existing game across language, platform or medium. Use for an unresolved whole or a cross-system change; skip isolated action, clue, scene, price, participation or content tasks with an established purpose, and purely technical changes that preserve game relations.

interface.shortDescription: Compose playable games across connected design domains

skills.name: game-design:game-information-design
skills.description: Create or revise puzzles, investigations, hidden-state reasoning, learning episodes, hints and external memory. Use when a game decision depends on available evidence, understanding, a teachable relation or assistance. Skip ordinary text edits, pure lore and tasks with no change to inference, learning or the work delegated to help.

interface.shortDescription: Create inference, learning and appropriate game help
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-information-design to construct the evidence, learning episode or help that this game decision needs.

skills.name: game-design:game-participation-design
skills.description: Design or revise shared play, player authority, matchmaking, access, assistance, intensity, departure, return and paid or timed rights. Use when who can know, choose, act, pay or continue changes the game. Skip developer-team coordination, generic account administration, clinical advice, legal compliance and financial forecasting.

interface.shortDescription: Design shared play, access, return and timed rights
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-participation-design to make this group's participation and next decisions executable.

skills.name: game-design:game-systems-design
skills.description: Design or revise game resources, prices, storage, exchange, progression, loss, recovery and state transfer across attempts, rosters, seasons or rule versions. Use when these rules change an actor's available plans. Skip purely cosmetic counters, business forecasts, generic database migrations and the agent's own task continuity.

interface.shortDescription: Design resources, progression and game state transfer
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-systems-design to revise this game economy and show each affected actor's next available plan.

skills.name: game-design:game-world-narrative-design
skills.description: Create or revise world relationships, places, inhabitants, playable scenes, dialogue, quests and conditional narrative. Use when actions should reveal a world or carry dramatic consequences across states and time. Skip copyediting, lore cataloguing without a design change and purely technical storage work; a world without a story need not use narrative procedures.

interface.shortDescription: Create encounterable worlds and consequential scenes
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-world-narrative-design to make a usable world fragment or scene with coherent actions and consequences.

skills.name: game-design:gameplay-design
skills.description: Create or revise game actions, controls, actor behavior and knowledge, spaces, encounters, shared timing, or free audiovisual play. Use for an executable action contract, behavior, layout, encounter or controllable phrase. Skip pure economy, lore, subscription policy, technical refactors and wording changes that leave these game relationships unchanged.

interface.shortDescription: Create actions, behaviors, spaces and playable timing
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $gameplay-design to create or revise the relevant playable relationship and deliver its concrete artifact.

skills.name: qualification-sentinel:qualification-sentinel
skills.description: Report the disposable lifecycle marker when explicitly requested.

skills.name: imagegen
skills.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

interface.shortDescription: Generate or edit images for websites, games, and more

Use when a game decision depends on available evidence, understanding, a teachable relation or assistance. Skip ordinary text edits, pure lore and tasks with no change to inference, learning or the work delegated to help.

interface.shortDescription: Create inference, learning and appropriate game help
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-information-design to construct the evidence, learning episode or help that this game decision needs.

skills.name: game-design:game-participation-design
skills.description: Design or revise shared play, player authority, matchmaking, access, assistance, intensity, departure, return and paid or timed rights. Use when who can know, choose, act, pay or continue changes the game. Skip developer-team coordination, generic account administration, clinical advice, legal compliance and financial forecasting.

interface.shortDescription: Design shared play, access, return and timed rights
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-participation-design to make this group's participation and next decisions executable.

skills.name: game-design:game-systems-design
skills.description: Design or revise game resources, prices, storage, exchange, progression, loss, recovery and state transfer across attempts, rosters, seasons or rule versions. Use when these rules change an actor's available plans. Skip purely cosmetic counters, business forecasts, generic database migrations and the agent's own task continuity.

interface.shortDescription: Design resources, progression and game state transfer
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-systems-design to revise this game economy and show each affected actor's next available plan.

skills.name: game-design:game-world-narrative-design
skills.description: Create or revise world relationships, places, inhabitants, playable scenes, dialogue, quests and conditional narrative. Use when actions should reveal a world or carry dramatic consequences across states and time. Skip copyediting, lore cataloguing without a design change and purely technical storage work; a world without a story need not use narrative procedures.

interface.shortDescription: Create encounterable worlds and consequential scenes
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $game-world-narrative-design to make a usable world fragment or scene with coherent actions and consequences.

skills.name: game-design:gameplay-design
skills.description: Create or revise game actions, controls, actor behavior and knowledge, spaces, encounters, shared timing, or free audiovisual play. Use for an executable action contract, behavior, layout, encounter or controllable phrase. Skip pure economy, lore, subscription policy, technical refactors and wording changes that leave these game relationships unchanged.

interface.shortDescription: Create actions, behaviors, spaces and playable timing
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $gameplay-design to create or revise the relevant playable relationship and deliver its concrete artifact.

skills.name: qualification-sentinel:qualification-sentinel
skills.description: Report the disposable lifecycle marker when explicitly requested.

skills.name: imagegen
skills.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

interface.shortDescription: Generate or edit images for websites, games, and more
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $imagegen to make or edit an image for this project.
